threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You keep staring at the bus schedule, waiting for a train, not realising you just have to hop on the 38 to get anywhere in Dalston.
Last night on the 59, a guy serenaded the whole bus with an off-key rendition of 'Wonderwall'—even got a round of applause at Brixton Station.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: It hit me when I heard the spontaneous dance party in the park while the buses were on strike. Only here do people turn a delay into a celebration.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg can you find a flea market where you can trade your old vinyl for homemade hummus. No cash needed, just good vibes.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can spot a local by their utter frustration with Muni delays, especially when it’s always a dog on the tracks causing chaos. Classic SF.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy in a suit reading Shakespeare on the 19 while a street musician belted out blues. Only in SF does chaos feel like art.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think they can just order a ‘café con leche’ at any hour. Local wisdom? It’s a morning drink, after 12, stick with a ‘cortado’.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: They often stand staring at the map on Carrer del Bisbe, oblivious to the locals weaving around them with purpose.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still think it's normal to complain about the weather in late April—it’s just a rite of passage here.
Caught a guy in a full penguin suit on the 196 last Saturday. He was practicing his waddle, claiming it was for a charity event. Only in Brixton!

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The day I saw my neighbor negotiating a peace treaty between two street cats over a patch of sun—this is home.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Friedrichshain can you sip coffee while watching spontaneous techno parties erupt in the streets, complete with glow sticks and eccentric dance moves.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know someone’s a local when they instinctively step over the coffee spill on the sidewalk instead of avoiding it. It’s just part of the scene.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Nothing like a dog on the tracks at Civic Center to slow everyone down—just another day in SF where even the pups have to make their mark.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think Gràcia is all about the plaça, but the real charm is in the little streets where locals barter for fresh produce. It's a different world.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can always tell by their hesitation at the menu—struggling with the Catalan names while the locals are already ordering with ease.
